parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Two properties of an ideal operational amplifier (op-amp) are infinite input impedance and infinite bandwidth.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
A student uses a negative temperature coefficient thermistor in the circuit of Fig. 7.1 to indicate changes in temperature.

{{figure:figure_7_1.png}}

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Show that the potential at point $X$ is $0.40\text{ V}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.stem: The thermistor has a resistance of $360\text{ k}\Omega$ at a particular temperature.
parts.text: For this temperature of the thermistor, calculate the magnitude of the reading on the voltmeter.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.stem: The temperature of the thermistor increases.
parts.text: State and explain the effect of this change on the magnitude of the reading on the voltmeter.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Explain why the amplifier circuit will no longer indicate temperature changes when the magnitude of the gain of the circuit is greater than $12.5$.
